references.text: Repeats the command to observe the Feast of Unleavened Bread as a permanent statute throughout all generations.
Confirms that the Passover regulation is to be observed as a permanent ordinance for the Israelites and their descendants.
The Passover is to serve as a sign and reminder that the Lord brought the people out of Egypt with a strong hand.
Sets the time for the Lord's Passover in the first month, as part of the annual festivals.
Command to celebrate the Passover at the appointed time as an annual memorial festival.
Restatement of the Passover regulation with provisions for the festival in the first month.
The command to keep the Passover as a memorial festival of the exodus from Egypt, all the days of one's life.
The Israelites celebrated the Passover after entering the Promised Land, fulfilling the permanent statute.
King Josiah kept the Passover for the Lord in Jerusalem, a renewal of the permanent statute.
Jesus and his disciples celebrated the Passover meal, showing the continuity of Passover observance into the New Testament.
Jesus institutes the Lord's Supper during the Passover meal with the words 'do this in remembrance of me', linking the aspect of remembrance to the new covenant.
Paul calls Christ our Passover lamb and urges believers to keep the festival, showing the fulfillment of the meaning of Passover in Christ.
The Lord's Supper as a memorial act ('do this in remembrance of me') reflects the function of Passover as זִכָּרוֹן (memorial).
Leviticus 23:41 specifies the duration and timing of the permanent festival ordinance established in Exodus 12:14.
Leviticus 23:21 elaborates on the requirement for a holy assembly and rest for the same festival established in Exodus 12:14.
